## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Tuvaṭakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 14) is the fourteenth text of the canonical *Mahāniddesa* in the Khuddaka Nikāya of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text constitutes an early canonical commentary and doctrinal exposition of the *Tuvaṭaka Sutta* from the *Aṭṭhakavagga* of the *Sutta Nipāta* [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records two modern translations across two languages [SuttaCentral]. Its traditional exegetical commentary is preserved in the *Mahāniddesa-aṭṭhakathā*, with which it shares substantial textual overlap [DharmaNexus].
The text exhibits extensive formulaic and exegetical parallels across early Buddhist literature. Curated passage-level parallels identified by SuttaCentral include other *Niddesa* treatises such as the *Sāriputtasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 16), *Purābhedasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 10), *Tissametteyyasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 7), *Kāmasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 1), and *Guhaṭṭhakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 2), as well as several sections of the *Cullaniddesa* (e.g., Cnd 8, Cnd 19, Cnd 23), the *Milindapañha* (Mil 7.2.4), and the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 1.1, Ps 1.4) [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus confirms this wide distribution, identifying 11,960 matching passages across 344 Pali texts, with the largest volumes of reuse found in Mnd 16 (§57.3–70.1 ↔ §23.1–36.1), Mnd 10 (§186.2–197.16 ↔ §47.2–59.2_8), Cnd 23 (§71.5–92.1 ↔ §97.1–118.1), and Mnd 15 [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus identifies machine-computed cross-language alignments with non-Pali corpora, including the Sanskrit *Saṅghabhedavastu*, the *Śrāvakabhūmi* section of the *Yogācārabhūmi* (in both Sanskrit and Tibetan), the Tibetan *Vinayakṣudrakavastu*, Nāgārjuna's *Dharmasaṃgraha*, and the *Arthaviniścayasūtra* [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
